text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- New finance minister Rolandas Matiliauskas sent his letter of resignation to Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, saying he wanted to end speculation over allegations he took a loan on preferential terms from a bank that later went bankrupt.

- One month has passed since a shopkeeper in the crime-ridden northern town of Panevezhys shot and killed four men and injured three others as they tried to extort money from him. But many questions remain unanswered so far.
- The bull run on the Lithuanian bourse calmed down and the market is waiting for the annual reports of companies.
- State loans commission declined to issue guarantees to Hermis Bank and Lithuanian Savings Banks for $16 million one-year credit for Lietuvos Energija energy company.
- The prosecutor's office has become interested in two other credits taken by ex-finance minister Rolandas Matiliauskas while working for a commercial bank.
- State audit officials say that the State Commercial Bank passed its most profitable loans to Tauras bank and in return accepted obligations for the bad loans TB issued in 1993.
- The confederation of industrialists asks Lithuanian lawmakers and government to grant private firms more legal rights to form security organisations of their own to fight growing organised crime.
- The finance ministry says its main task is to create a clear and stable tax law.

- The recent growing interest in Lithuanian shares is due to a stable political situation, the growing interest of foreign investors and the gap between the real and market value of shares, bourse experts say.

- The head of a delegation of Russian industrialists and businessman, Arkadi Volski, said during his visit to Vilnius that the projects of Lithuanian and Russian companies which are being created are worth hundreds rather than tens of millions of dollars.
- The government approved partial support to the export of meat and dairy products.
- The gross profit of Lithuanian industry and service companies was estimated at 442 million litas during the third quarter of 1996.
